question.prompt:
What is the value in simplest form of the following expression?

\[ \begin{aligned} &\sqrt{1} + \sqrt{1+3} + \sqrt{1+3+5} \\ &\quad {}+ \sqrt{1+3+5+7} \end{aligned} \]

solutions.title: Evaluate the square roots
solutions.explanation:
The sums inside the radicals are small perfect squares, so calculate those sums first.

The four radicands are \(1\), \(1+3=4\), \(1+3+5=9\), and \(1+3+5+7=16\). Their nonnegative square roots give
\[
\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{4}+\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{16}
=1+2+3+4=10.
\]
Therefore the value is \(\boxed{10}\), choice \(\textbf{C}\).
